what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Senegal in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 22107 Senegalese asylum seekers in the United States, 56.7% of all asylum seekers from Senegal.
Refugees from Senegal, a separate group, live mostly in France, Gambia, Canada and Italy.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over Casamance territory in Senegal in some years from 1995 to 2011, with the MFDC in 2003 and 2011.
The fact pack records no armed conflict in Senegal in recent years, so it does not say why the number of asylum seekers grew.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 136 asylum seekers.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2024 and 2025, and the figure is at its highest at the end of 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
